cx 0.5.0 turns cx from a way to open one Claude Code session on a server into a way to run many of them at once — across servers, branches and conversations — and always know which one needs you. Sessions can now share a project's files or get a worktree of their own, report whether they are working, finished or waiting on a permission prompt, and be steered, grouped under a goal, or left to drive themselves.

Claude still runs only on your servers, and the client still holds no credentials.

![cx 0.5.0](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/farajzadeh/cx/v0.5.0/docs/media/hero.gif)

## Highlights

### Pick instead of type

Leave the target out at a terminal and cx offers a menu of what that command can act on — fzf if you have it, a built-in menu if you don't. Scripts see exactly the old behaviour.

![Picking a target](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/farajzadeh/cx/v0.5.0/docs/media/picker.gif)

### `cx find`

Every project, worktree and live session on every server in one menu, then what to do with it: open, shell, peek, nudge, stop, or a new `@session` on the same files. `cx find --print` just prints the choice, so `cx ask "$(cx find --print api)" "..."` works.

![cx find](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/farajzadeh/cx/v0.5.0/docs/media/find.gif)

### Create and open in one step

`cx new web1:api --open` and `cx wt add web1:api/authfix --open` create and attach. Run bare at a terminal, both ask for what is missing.

![Create and open](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/farajzadeh/cx/v0.5.0/docs/media/create-open.gif)

### Listings you can narrow

`cx ls web` for everything matching "web", `--live`, `--active 2h`, `--idle 7d`, `--dirty`, `--group host`, `--sort active`. `cx host ls --down` shows which servers didn't answer. Plain `cx ls` prints exactly what it always did.

![Filtering cx ls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/farajzadeh/cx/v0.5.0/docs/media/ls-filter.gif)

### Completion that knows your targets

Rewritten for bash, zsh (plus an oh-my-zsh plugin) and fish: projects, then worktrees and `@labels`, only running sessions for `stop` and `nudge`, and a flag list for every command. `cx completion bash|zsh|fish` prints the script, and `install.sh` links it into place.

![Shell completion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/farajzadeh/cx/v0.5.0/docs/media/completion.gif)

### Parallel work that can't collide

`cx open web1:api@review` is a second conversation on the same files; `cx wt add web1:api/authfix` is a branch and directory of its own. Every session pins its own Claude conversation, so two sessions on one project no longer resume — and corrupt — the same one. `cx wt rm web1:api --merged` cleans up afterwards.

![Parallel sessions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/farajzadeh/cx/v0.5.0/docs/media/parallel.gif)

### See which session needs you, and answer it

`cx peek` says whether each session is idle, working, blocked on a permission prompt, starting or dead; `cx nudge` types the next prompt into one that is ready. `cx bar`, `cx tabs` and `cx jump` put the same answer in your tmux status line and tabs, and the server's own tmux bar shows context use, cost and usage limits. `cx goal` records a definition of done, and `cx goal on-stop` lets a goal drive itself.

![Peek and nudge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/farajzadeh/cx/v0.5.0/docs/media/peek-nudge.gif)

## Upgrading

1. Update the client. From a clone:

   ```sh
   git pull && ./install.sh
   ```

   or re-run the one-liner:

   ```sh
   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/farajzadeh/cx/main/install.sh | bash
   ```

   `cx --version` should print `cx 0.5.0`.

2. Update the agent on every server:

   ```sh
   cx provision --all
   ```

   Nothing on the servers is lost — projects, sessions and conversations stay where they are. Until a server is updated, the commands from 0.1.0 keep working against it, newer ones say which server is too old and how to fix it, and `cx doctor` marks it.

3. Optionally, `cx bar --setup` prints the tmux lines for the status bar, tab icons and `prefix + j`.

## Behaviour changes

- **`cx ls <word>`**: a word that is not a configured host is now a pattern. A mistyped host gives an empty listing with exit `0`, where it used to be an error with exit `2`.
- **A missing target opens a menu at a terminal**, and cancelling it exits `130`. Without a terminal, or under `--json`, `-y` or `CX_PICKER=none`, commands still exit `3` as before.
- **Bare `cx new` and `cx wt add` ask questions at a terminal**, including whether to open the result (`CX_OPEN_AFTER_CREATE=ask|always|never`).
- **Exiting Claude ends the session** instead of leaving a shell on the server. Use `cx shell` for a shell.
- **Each session keeps its own conversation.** The first open after upgrading adopts the conversation it would have resumed before.
- **`cx ask` refuses a running session** with exit `4`; use `cx nudge` to talk to it.
- **`cx open` passes Claude per-session hooks and a status line.** Your `settings.json` is untouched and your own `statusLine` still runs; `--no-hooks` and `CX_SERVER_BAR=0` opt out.
- **`cx peek` counts finished sessions rather than listing them**; `--all` lists them, `--json` is unchanged.

Full details, including everything fixed: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/farajzadeh/cx/blob/v0.5.0/CHANGELOG.md).
